title: Redwood All-Hands - December 2026 Leadership Update
summary: Leadership gave a year-end update: strong revenue growth, Dedicated bookings exceeded targets, Private deployments pilot underway with two enterprise customers, product roadmap focuses on observability and lower-latency kernels, hiring slowed but targeted senior IC recruiting continues. Noted a recent SRE incident that revealed gaps in tracing; action items assigned. Culture roundup and offsite highlights. Next steps include sharing detailed FY27 hiring plan, product milestones doc, and SRE postmortem.
next_steps: Priya to share SRE incident postmortem by 2027-01-05
Samuel to send Q1 2027 roadmap deck to the company by 2026-12-31
People Ops to publish updated hiring plan and open roles by 2027-01-07
Sales to circulate Dedicated contract template and case studies next week
action_items: Priya Kapoor: produce SRE incident postmortem and mitigation plan; due 2027-01-05
Lina Park: assess kernel rollout cadence and escalate resource needs; due 2027-01-10
Jordan Reyes: compile Dedicated/Private customer wins and references; due 2027-01-03

transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-12-29
Time: 10:00 AM PST
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Ava (CEO), Marcus (COO), Priya (CTO), Samuel (VP Product), Lina (Head Eng), Jordan (Head Sales), plus all employees on livestream

[00:00] Ava: Good morning everyone, uh, thanks for joining our year end, leadership update. I know it's a busy week, appreciate you carving out the time. We have, um, about an hour, gonna run through topline metrics, product highlights, and then open for q&a. Marcus, want to kick off with the numbers?

[00:35] Marcus: Yeah thanks Ava. Quick callout, revenue growth this year, we ended up at 3.4x ARR growth relative to last year, bookings for Dedicated exceeded plan by 18 percent which was a big driver. Some of that came from a handful of expansion deals that closed late Q3 and Q4. Net retention stayed healthy, roughly 112 percent, churn is slightly higher in self-serve SMB segment, so we're looking at retention initiatives in Q1.

[01:20] Jordan: i'll add, on the sales side we saw a big lift from the new case study with Fathom Health — that deal helped normalize our messaging for regulated verticals, and the Dedicated offering with VPC and KMS really opened doors in healthcare and finance.

[02:05] Priya: technical signal — we shipped the 2.1 runtime with improved continuous batching; customers are seeing 10-15 percent lower p99 latency for typical chat flows, measured on our internal benchmarks. There's still windows where kv cache warmups cause spikes, which ties into the incident we had last month.

[02:45] Ava: right let's talk about that incident briefly, because it's important for trust. Priya, can you summarize?

[03:00] Priya: Sure. On 2026-12-03 we had a regression during a kernel rollout that caused a partial outage for Dedicated clusters in us-west. It was traced to an ordering bug in the kernel selection layer, combined with an edge-case in autoscaler heuristics. We paged, mitigated with a rollback, and restored service in ~80 minutes. Impact was limited but customer-facing and not great. We're doing a full postmortem; immediate actions are spaced rollouts, stronger pre-rollout simulation, and added tracing in kernel selector.

[03:45] Marcus: Important to note we honored SLA credits proactively for affected customers and legal handled comms. We'll need to ensure the credits and comms are documented for future audits.

[04:20] Samuel: On the product roadmap, Q1 priorities are: 1) Observability improvements — token-level tracing and rollbacks, 2) Cost/perf toolkit enhancements — smarter quantization recommendations and workload-based batching presets, 3) Private deployment stabilization — easier install and better KMS integrations. I'll share a detailed deck after this.

[05:05] Lina: From eng operations, we're focusing on the kernel rollout process — adding staged canaries and better perf gates. Also investing in our test harness to better simulate mixed workloads. Hiring constraints mean we need to prioritize where we add heads; plan is to hire 2 senior infra engineers and a performance SWE in Q1.

[05:45] Ava: hiring — can you summarize top roles? People Ops?

[06:00] Samuel: top roles: senior infra eng, SRE manager, two backend perf leads, and a product manager for Dedicated. We are being selective, not just headcount growth.

[06:30] Jordan: customer highlights — we launched pilots with two large customers on Private (name withheld for NDA), and Dedicated expansion with Finity Bank closed at the end of Nov; these are strategic references. I'll push out the case study drafts next week.

[07:10] Ava: great. A note on compliance — we finished SOC 2 re-audit prep and expect final signoff in Jan, and we also have a renewed interest from EU customers around data residency, so the Private EU region initiative is on track.

[07:45] Employee Q (via chat): Any plan to lower hosted API latency for long-context models?

[08:00] Priya: yes, long-context work is a priority; we're exploring chunked attention kernels and also better KV eviction heuristics so inferring with long histories doesn't degrade other tenants. There will be perf tradeoffs; we may gate some of this behind Dedicated or premium tiers initially.

[08:40] Marcus: On finance, burn is within plan for Q4 but we are tightening runway targets for FY27 until we see steady ramp in enterprise renewals. Revenue mix shifting toward higher-margin Dedicated helps unit economics.

[09:15] Ava: culture/offsite recap — last week's leadership offsite in Santa Cruz was useful. Quick takeaways: folks want clearer prioritization, more cross-team demos, and a better onboarding flow. We're launching a 'mission days' program to surface cross-functional demos quarterly.

[10:00] Priya: quick technical deep dive snippet — kernel selector now has a fallback path to a quantized variant; this has reduced cost for embeddings-heavy workloads by ~30 percent in tests, but we need more validation in production.

[10:40] Employee Q: will we open-source performance tooling?

[10:50] Samuel: we plan to open-source some of the benchmarking harness and guidance to help customers reproduce our numbers, but not internal kernel code or proprietary optimizations. That helps developer adoption and trust.

[11:20] Jordan: sales ops is preparing a new Dedicated pricing template for AR and retail customers; it'll be in the sales wiki by Jan 4.

[11:40] Priya: on Private deployments, the on-prem package now supports HSM-backed KMS and improved audit logs; initial installs took longer than expected so we're streamlining the installer and adding more automation to reduce time-to-first-pilot.

[12:15] Marcus: ops improvement — we will centralize support SLAs and create runbooks for common Private install failures.

[12:50] Ava: ok let's run a quick Q&A from the chat and live mic.

[13:10] Employee (mic): curious about Q2 targets — are we being aggressive?

[13:20] Marcus: we'll share targets in January; expect modest growth assumed in Q1 while we invest in product and ops. Q2 will be more aggressive when recruitment completes and the Dedicated pipeline converts.

[14:00] Employee (mic): any update on partner ecosystem?

[14:10] Jordan: exploring partnerships with a couple of cloud vendors and SI partners; also trials with a vector db partner to better integrate embedding workflows.

[14:45] Priya: ops note — we will run a staged kernel rollout in Jan with a small customer cohort to validate the new selector logic. Details in the postmortem.

[15:15] Ava: closing remarks — big thanks to the teams, we shipped major runtime improvements and enterprise traction this year. We'll be focused and deliberate in hiring and delivery next year. Look out for the roadmap deck and postmortem links. Happy holidays everyone.

[15:45] Meeting closed.

Notes on transcription quality: auto-generated captions with some word swaps (e.g., kv cache sometimes transcribed as 'kayv cache'); speaker markers are mostly accurate but a few chat questions merged into transcript.
